<reason>Both sides built coherent, well-structured cases, but PRO's economic mechanism (scarce road space, queuing, health/reliability gains) was clearer and its use of real-world examples held up better under scrutiny. CON's strongest weapon was the "Stockholm gotcha" — forcing PRO to admit a trial-plus-later-vote model and then claiming this concedes CON's sequencing framework. But this conflates two different things: CON's opening explicitly demanded consent *precede* imposition, while Stockholm's referendum came *after* imposition, ratifying lived results — exactly PRO's retrospective-consent theory, which PRO stated plainly ("The vote that matters comes after the streets move, not before"). CON's other core examples were also weaker than presented: Edinburgh and Manchester never implemented pricing at all, so they illustrate what happens when a referendum-first approach is followed and fails, arguably undercutting CON's own prescription rather than supporting it; and PRO correctly noted NYC's plan eventually went live despite the governor's pause, turning CON's collapse narrative into a story of temporary wavering rather than proof of fragility. PRO also handled the pressure questions cleanly (labeled A1/A2, direct answers) and offered a sharper reframe on equity (time-cost vs. cash-cost) that CON never fully neutralized. CON's closing landed the last word with a confident "that's CON's case, not theirs" framing, but on inspection this overstates what PRO conceded. Overall PRO's case was more internally consistent and better supported by accurate use of examples, giving it a clear, if not overwhelming, edge.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The Stockholm exchange: CON's attempt to trap PRO's "trial plus later vote" concession as secretly endorsing CON's pre-imposition consent model, versus PRO's rejoinder distinguishing retrospective ratification ("vote after streets move") from CON's demand for consent before imposition — this is the pivotal clash, and PRO's distinction survives closer scrutiny better than CON's conflation.</best_rebuttal>
